notes: §1985:IX.4.4.4 GR14: when the I-O phrase is specified and label records are present, "The labels are checked in accordance with the implementor's specified conventions for input-output label checking" and "The new labels are written in accordance with the implementor's specified conventions for input-output label writing". Both steps are implementor-defined (§1985:C.2 item 61 names this rule: "The labels are checked or written in accordance with the implementor's specified conventions for input or output label handling"). The implementation's convention is that a file carries no label the COBOL program can see: labels belong to the host file system (§1985:C.1: "Specifying the presence of file labels is considered a function of the operating system and as such does not belong in the COBOL program"), and docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md Table 7 row 7.4 states it as 'accepted-inert at 85'. The clause is parsed at 85 (FileDescriptionFormats.Rows admits it in every FD format; VersionConformancePass.VisitLabelRecordsClause refuses it from 2002, COBOL0902) and no binder or runtime member reads it, so the I-O arm of KeyedConnector.OpenCore attaches the existing store and checks and writes no label, which is the whole of the convention. Probed at --std 85: OPEN I-O answers 00 under STANDARD and with no clause, and the READ and REWRITE that follow succeed. The witness opens a LABEL RECORDS ARE STANDARD indexed file I-O (status 00), reads its record and rewrites it. Not covered by this verdict: the clause's own syntax is unchecked at 85 (kb/Work PB5070), and docs/CONFORMANCE.md has no entry for the 1985 implementor-defined list's label items (§1985:C.2 items 60 and 61), so the convention is written down only in the VCR row.

next.reason: 1985: "When the I-O phrase is specified and the LABEL RECORDS clause indicates label records are present... labels are checked"; 2023: "OPEN rules (e.g. GR-14.9.27.4-16 on the I-O phrase) state no label checking or writing; no candidate mentions LABEL RECORDS". 2023 OPEN rules cover the I-O phrase but say nothing of label records or label checking and writing. The LABEL RECORDS feature is absent from the candidates, so the requirement is dropped.
